answer: An AI-agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with bonded unique-identity attestations: each agent locks a stake before its vote counts, and a verifier samples accounts and follows their funding trail. Any two accounts traced to one controller lose the whole bond. A fake sparrow account made to harvest rewards is costly, since the attacker must post fresh collateral for every identity and one caught clone burns the deposit and blacklists the wallet. Even an oasis of clones faces a rising tide of required stake, so cost grows linearly with the attack while an honest agent pays once.
